topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It provides introductory framing for the lecture and sets expectations regarding complement nomenclature.

topics.label: Principles and core logic of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce the fundamental organization, naming rules, and central C3 activation reaction of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the three distinct recognition pathways that initiate the complement cascade and converge to form C3 convertases.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream biological processes by which activated complement targets and eliminates pathogens.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation on host tissues to avoid self-damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details how deficiencies at different stages of the complement cascade produce distinct clinical pathologies and infection susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and biotechnology applications
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how pathogens circumvent complement-mediated clearance and how bacterial evasion factors are utilized in biomedical tools.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture by concluding the module and outlining the topic of the upcoming session.
